He served as a bulletin writer for the Grand Army at Caseros and later broke with Urquiza. As governor of San Juan he led the 1863 war against the Chacho Peñaloza. He was president (1868–1874), promoted public education and immigration, and in Conflict and Harmony of the Races in America (1883) he explained American history through racial factors.

personas/jose-hernandez/resumen.texto: Federalist writer, journalist and politician from Buenos Aires Province, author of Martín Fierro. He defended the frontier gauchos, opposed the governments of Mitre and Sarmiento and in 1880 supported the federalization of Buenos Aires.

hechos/invencion-de-la-escritura-cuneifo.texto: The oldest tablets, found in Uruk, are administrative records with pictographic signs. From that system derived cuneiform writing, which was used for more than three millennia.

hechos/reinado-de-hammurabi/resumen.texto: Hammurabi inherits a minor kingdom and within three decades subdues Larsa, Mari and Eshnunna. Toward the end of his reign he has his law code engraved.

hechos/caida-de-ninive/resumen.texto: A coalition of Babylonians and Medes sacks the Assyrian capital, leading to the disappearance of the Neo-Assyrian Empire.

hechos/toma-de-babilonia-por-ciro/titulo.texto: Capture of Babylon by Cyrus II

hechos/toma-de-babilonia-por-ciro/resume.texto: Cyrus the Great enters Babylon without much resistance and ends the Neo-Babylonian Empire. Mesopotamia becomes part of the Achaemenid Empire.

hechos/destruccion-del-primer-templo/tit.texto: Fall of Jerusalem and destruction of the First Temple

hechos/destruccion-del-primer-templo/res.texto: Nebuchadnezzar II takes Jerusalem, destroys the Temple and deports part of the population of Judah to Babylon. The date varies between 587 and 586 BC.

hechos/destruccion-del-segundo-templo/re.texto: Titus takes Jerusalem after a siege and the legions set fire to the Temple. It is the central event of the Jewish–Roman war recounted by Josephus.

hechos/conquista-musulmana-de-siria/resu.texto: The armies of the Rashidun Caliphate defeat the Byzantines at the Battle of the Yarmouk (636) and conquer Syria and Palestine. Jerusalem surrenders c. 637–638.

hechos/primera-cruzada-jerusalen/titulo.texto: Capture of Jerusalem by the crusaders

hechos/primera-cruzada-jerusalen/resumen.texto: After a five-week siege, the crusaders took Jerusalem on 15 July 1099 and killed a large part of its Muslim and Jewish inhabitants: the Latin chroniclers speak of blood up to the ankles or knees on the Temple Mount, and Ibn al-Athir of 70,000 dead, a figure historians consider exaggerated. A letter from the Jewish community of Egypt confirms the massacre and the ransoming of captives. The victors founded the Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem.

hechos/batalla-de-hattin/resumen.texto: On 4 July 1187 Saladin surrounded the army of the Kingdom of Jerusalem, without water, at the Horns of Hattin, above the Sea of Galilee. King Guy was captured, Raynald of Châtillon executed and the captured Templars and Hospitallers beheaded. Without an army, the kingdom lost almost all its cities, and Jerusalem itself, within a few months.

hechos/caida-de-troya/resumen.texto: Stratum VIIa at Hisarlik shows a violent destruction c. 1180 BC. It is debated whether it is related to the Trojan War narrated in the Iliad.

hechos/caida-de-lidia/titulo.texto: Conquest of Lydia by Cyrus II

hechos/caida-de-lidia/resumen.texto: Cyrus defeats Croesus and takes Sardis. The Greek cities of the coast come under Persian rule.

hechos/concilio-de-nicea/resumen.texto: Convened by Constantine, it brings together bishops from across the empire to settle the Arian controversy and establish the Nicene Creed.

hechos/batalla-de-manzikert/resumen.texto: The Seljuk sultan Alp Arslan defeats and captures the Byzantine emperor Romanos IV Diogenes. The battle opens Anatolia to Turkish penetration.

hechos/republica-de-turquia/titulo.texto: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

hechos/republica-de-turquia/resumen.texto: After the War of Independence and the Treaty of Lausanne, Mustafa Kemal proclaims the republic on 29 October.

hechos/batalla-de-maraton/resumen.texto: The Athenians and Plataeans defeat the Persian army of Darius I on the plain of Marathon, during the First Persian War.

hechos/batalla-de-salamina/resumen.texto: The Greek fleet, commanded by Themistocles, destroys the Persian fleet of Xerxes I in the strait of Salamis.

hechos/guerra-del-peloponeso/resumen.texto: War between the Delian League, led by Athens, and the Peloponnesian League, led by Sparta. It ended with the surrender of Athens in 404 BC.

hechos/batalla-de-queronea/resumen.texto: Philip II of Macedon defeats Athens and Thebes and secures his hegemony over Greece.

hechos/destruccion-de-corinto/resumen.texto: The consul Lucius Mummius sacks and razes Corinth at the end of the Achaean War. Greece becomes a Roman province.

hechos/fundacion-de-roma/resumen.texto: According to the tradition recorded by Livy, Romulus founds the city in 753 BC. Archaeology confirms settlements on the Palatine from the 8th century BC.

hechos/inicio-de-la-republica-romana/res.texto: According to tradition, the expulsion of the last king, Tarquin the Proud, gives way to government by two annual consuls.

hechos/asesinato-de-julio-cesar/resumen.texto: On 15 March 44 BC, a group of senators stab Caesar. His death reopens the civil wars and leads to the rise of Octavian.

hechos/erupcion-del-vesubio/resumen.texto: The eruption buries Pompeii, Herculaneum and Stabiae. Pliny the Younger described the event in his letters to Tacitus.

hechos/caida-del-imperio-de-occidente/re.texto: The Germanic leader Odoacer deposes the young emperor Romulus Augustulus and sends the imperial insignia to Constantinople. It is the conventional date for the end of the Western Roman Empire.

hechos/victoria-de-ciro-sobre-astiages/t.texto: Cyrus II defeats the king of the Medes

hechos/victoria-de-ciro-sobre-astiages/r.texto: Cyrus defeats Astyages, the last king of the Medes, and unites Medes and Persians. It is considered the beginning of the Achaemenid Empire.

hechos/ascenso-de-dario-i/resumen.texto: After the death of Cambyses II, Darius defeats Gaumata and rebels throughout the empire and has himself crowned king. He documents this himself at Behistun.

hechos/incendio-de-persepolis/resumen.texto: Alexander the Great sacks Persepolis and the palace is set on fire.

hechos/batalla-de-nahavand/resumen.texto: The forces of the Rashidun Caliphate destroy the Sasanian army; the empire collapses. The last emperor, Yazdegerd III, dies in 651.

hechos/safavidas-ismail-i/titulo.texto: Ismail I founds the Safavid dynasty

hechos/safavidas-ismail-i/resumen.texto: Ismail I proclaims himself shah in Tabriz and declares Twelver Shi'ism the state religion, which changed the religious history of Iran.

hechos/unificacion-de-china-por-qin/resu.texto: The king of Qin conquers the last of the rival kingdoms and proclaims himself first emperor. A centralized state with commanderies and standardization is established.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-dinastia-han/resu.texto: Liu Bang defeats Xiang Yu and proclaims himself Emperor Gaozu of Han. The Han will rule, with one interruption, until the year 220.

hechos/mision-de-zhang-qian/titulo.texto: Zhang Qian's mission to Central Asia

hechos/mision-de-zhang-qian/resumen.texto: Emperor Wu sends Zhang Qian to seek allies against the Xiongnu. He returns thirteen years later with news of Ferghana, Bactria and Parthia, and opens the way for the Silk Road.

hechos/invencion-del-papel/titulo.texto: Cai Lun presents paper to the Han court

hechos/invencion-del-papel/resumen.texto: According to tradition, the eunuch Cai Lun presents the emperor with paper made from bark and rags. Archaeological finds show older paper.

hechos/fundacion-de-la-dinastia-tang/res.texto: Li Yuan takes Chang'an and proclaims himself emperor. The Tang will rule until 907, in one of the periods of greatest cultural splendor in China.

hechos/batalla-del-hidaspes/resumen.texto: Alexander the Great defeats King Porus at the Hydaspes (Jhelum) River. Shortly afterward his troops refuse to continue eastward.

hechos/conquista-de-kalinga/resumen.texto: Ashoka conquests Kalinga with enormous loss of life. In Major Rock Edict XIII he expresses his remorse and turns to the policy of dhamma.

hechos/fundacion-del-imperio-gupta/resum.texto: Chandragupta I begins the Gupta dynasty; the year 320 is taken as the starting date of its era.

hechos/sultanato-de-delhi/resumen.texto: After the death of Muhammad of Ghor, his general Qutb ud-Din Aibak proclaims himself sultan, the beginning of the Turko-Afghan presence in northern India.

hechos/primera-batalla-de-panipat/resume.texto: Babur defeats Ibrahim Lodi, the last sultan of Delhi, and founds the Mughal Empire.

hechos/san-lorenzo-olmeca/resumen.texto: San Lorenzo is the first great Olmec center, with colossal basalt heads and hydraulic works. It is considered one of the first centers of power in Mesoamerica.

hechos/fundacion-de-tenochtitlan/resumen.texto: According to Mexica tradition, after their migration from Aztlán they founded their city on an islet in Lake Texcoco. The date is taken from the codices.

hechos/llegada-de-cortes-a-tenochtitlan/.texto: On 8 November 1519 Cortés and his allies are received by Moctezuma II on the Iztapalapa causeway.

hechos/caida-de-tenochtitlan/resumen.texto: On 13 August 1521 Cuauhtémoc surrenders after a three-month siege. Mexica rule comes to an end.

hechos/grito-de-dolores/resumen.texto: On 16 September 1810 the priest Miguel Hidalgo calls for an uprising against Spanish rule; the Mexican War of Independence begins.

hechos/auge-de-caral/resumen.texto: Caral, in the Supe Valley, is the largest known urban center of the Norte Chico civilization, with pyramids and sunken plazas; it is one of the oldest cities in the Americas.

hechos/expansion-inca-pachacutec/resumen.texto: According to Betanzos, Cieza and Sarmiento de Gamboa, after defeating the Chancas Pachacuti took power and began the great expansion of the Tawantinsuyu; Garcilaso attributes that victory to his father, Viracocha Inca. The dates come from oral tradition and from the chroniclers' chronologies.

hechos/captura-de-atahualpa/resumen.texto: On 16 November 1532 Pizarro and some 170 Spaniards capture Atahualpa and kill thousands of his followers. It is the decisive event of the conquest of Peru.

hechos/rebelion-de-tupac-amaru-ii/resume.texto: José Gabriel Condorcanqui, cacique of Tungasuca, rose up in November 1780 against the corregidores and the forced distribution of goods, and the rebellion spread through the Andean south and Upper Peru. He was defeated and executed in Cusco in May 1781, together with part of his family. The war and the repression left tens of thousands dead, according to estimates.

hechos/batalla-de-ayacucho/resumen.texto: On 9 December 1824, the forces of Antonio José de Sucre defeat the royalist army and end Spanish rule in South America.

hechos/primera-fundacion-de-buenos-aires.texto: Pedro de Mendoza founds Nuestra Señora Santa María del Buen Ayre. Hunger and war with the Querandíes weaken it, and in 1541 Domingo Martínez de Irala orders it depopulated and its residents taken to Asunción.

hechos/fundacion-de-asuncion/resumen.texto: Juan de Salazar de Espinosa founds the fort of Nuestra Señora Santa María de la Asunción, which becomes the center of Spanish rule.

hechos/segunda-fundacion-de-buenos-aires.texto: On 11 June, Juan de Garay founds the Ciudad de la Trinidad and the port of Santa María de los Buenos Aires.

hechos/revolucion-de-mayo/resumen.texto: The open cabildo of May 22 voted that Viceroy Cisneros should give up command. On the 24th the Cabildo formed a junta presided over by Cisneros himself, who resigned that night under pressure from the militias and the residents. On the 25th, faced with a petition from residents and military leaders, it recognized the First Junta presided over by Saavedra, which governed in the name of Ferdinand VII.

hechos/declaracion-de-independencia-1816.texto: Declaration of Independence of the United Provinces
On 9 July, the Congress of Tucumán proclaims the independence of the United Provinces in South America.

lugares/uruk/resumen.texto: Sumerian city of Gilgamesh, considered one of the world's first cities. The oldest tablets bearing writing appear there.

lugares/babilonia/resumen.texto: Capital of Hammurabi and of Nebuchadnezzar II. Its ruins lie next to present-day Hillah, in Iraq.

lugares/ninive/resumen.texto: Capital of the Neo-Assyrian Empire under Sennacherib and Ashurbanipal, with its great library of tablets. Opposite present-day Mosul.

lugares/jerusalen/resumen.texto: Holy city of Judaism, Christianity and Islam; its occupation dates back to the Bronze Age.

lugares/biblos/resumen.texto: Phoenician port, one of the oldest continuously inhabited settlements; cedar wood was shipped from there to Egypt.

lugares/tiro/resumen.texto: Great Phoenician port and mother city of colonies such as Carthage; Herodotus places its founding c. 2750 BC according to the local priests.

lugares/hattusa/resumen.texto: Capital of the Hittite Empire, at Boğazköy. Its royal archive of cuneiform tablets was discovered in 1906.

lugares/efeso/resumen.texto: Greek city of Ionia, home of the Artemision and later capital of the Roman province of Asia; Paul preached there.

lugares/troya/resumen.texto: Site of Hisarlik, with nine main strata; identified since Schliemann with the Troy of the Iliad.

lugares/atenas/resumen.texto: City-state, cradle of democracy and intellectual center of the 5th century BC; the Parthenon was built on the Acropolis.

lugares/esparta/resumen.texto: City-state of Laconia with a militaristic regime; rival of Athens and victor in the Peloponnesian War.

lugares/delfos/resumen.texto: Sanctuary of Apollo and seat of the most consulted oracle in the Greek world, until its closure under Theodosius. In 279 BC it withstood the attack of the Gauls led by Brennus (Pausanias X.19–23), and to celebrate this the Soteria festivals were founded.

lugares/roma/resumen.texto: Capital of the Roman Empire and seat of the papacy, on the banks of the Tiber.

lugares/ostia/resumen.texto: Port of Rome at the mouth of the Tiber, with very well-preserved ruins of streets, baths and warehouses.

lugares/pompeya/resumen.texto: Campanian city buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79; its excavation reveals the daily life of a Roman city.

lugares/persepolis/resumen.texto: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire begun by Darius I, near Shiraz. It was burned in 330 BC.

lugares/pasargadas/resumen.texto: First Achaemenid capital, founded by Cyrus II, whose tomb is there.

lugares/susa/resumen.texto: Ancient capital of Elam and Achaemenid administrative capital. The stele of the Code of Hammurabi was found there.

lugares/changan/resumen.texto: Capital of the Western Han, the Sui and the Tang, in present-day Xi'an; eastern end of the Silk Road.

lugares/luoyang/resumen.texto: Capital of the Eastern Zhou and the Eastern Han, by the Luo River; home to great Buddhist monasteries.

lugares/anyang/resumen.texto: Last Shang capital, where thousands of oracle bones bearing the oldest Chinese writing were found.

lugares/mohenjo-daro/resumen.texto: One of the largest cities of the Indus civilization, with grid-plan streets and drainage systems.

lugares/pataliputra/resumen.texto: Capital of the Maurya and Gupta empires, on the Ganges, in present-day Patna. Megasthenes described it as a great walled city.

lugares/varanasi/resumen.texto: Holy city of Hinduism on the banks of the Ganges; nearby is Sarnath, where the Buddha gave his first sermon.

lugares/tenochtitlan/resumen.texto: Mexica capital on an island in Lake Texcoco, beneath present-day Mexico City. Cortés described it in his letters.

lugares/teotihuacan/resumen.texto: Great city of the Central Highlands with the Pyramids of the Sun and the Moon. It reached tens of thousands of inhabitants and was burned c. 550.

lugares/chichen-itza/resumen.texto: Maya center in northern Yucatán, with the pyramid of Kukulcan and the largest ball court in Mesoamerica.

lugares/cusco/resumen.texto: Capital of Tawantinsuyu, the “navel of the world” for the Incas, today the center of Andean Peru.

lugares/machu-picchu/resumen.texto: 15th-century Inca llaqta, linked to the royal estate of Pachacuti, abandoned after the conquest.

lugares/caral/resumen.texto: City of the Norte Chico civilization in the Supe Valley, with monumental buildings more than 4,500 years old.

lugares/buenos-aires/resumen.texto: Capital of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata and of Argentina. Mendoza founded it in 1536 and Garay refounded it in 1580.

lugares/asuncion/resumen.texto: Capital of Paraguay; it was the center of the Spanish colonization of the Río de la Plata in the 16th century.

lugares/montevideo/resumen.texto: Port on the north coast of the estuary, founded between 1724 and 1726 by the governor of Buenos Aires, Bruno Mauricio de Zabala, to check Portuguese expansion. Today it is the capital of Uruguay.
